report.source_text: On the H&E-stained slides, a 4 mm tumour was found in the dermis. The tumour had a solid pattern in the centre and a more organoid pattern without any necrosis or mucin in the border of the tumour, deeper in the dermis (figure 1A). The tumour cells were fairly uniform with oval to round nuclei with dispersed chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli and eosinophilic and fine granular cytoplasm (figure 1B). The mitotic counts were 8 per 2 mm2.

report.source_text: The immunohistochemical staining was positive in the peripheral part of the tumour for synaptophysin, CD56, S-100 and SOX-10, special AT-rich sequence-binding protein 2 (SATB2), ISLET-1 and dot-like positive stain for pan cytokeratin (AE1/AE3). The centre of the tumour stained negative for synaptophysin but was partly positive for CD56, S-100 and SOX-10. Staining was negative for cytokeratin 7 (CK7), cytokeratin 20 (CK20), thyroid transcription factor-1 (TTF-1), melanoma antigen (Melan A), chromogranin A, CDX-2, serotonin, melanoma-specific antigen (MSA), microphthalmia transcription factor (MITF), CD45, CD3 and CD20. Furthermore, there was negative staining for Merkel Cell Polyomavirus (MCPyV). The KI-67 index varied but was up to 10% (figure 2).

clinician.current_trajectory_hypothesis: Late 30s male with 5-6 year history of 4mm painful subareolar skin nodule underwent excision by GP. H&E and IHC confirm low-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma with organoid pattern, synaptophysin/CD56 positivity, Ki-67 up to 10%, and negative Merkel cell polyomavirus. Distinction from Merkel cell carcinoma, melanoma (despite S-100/SOX-10 positivity), lymphoma, and metastatic carcinomas (lung/GI) supported by negative TTF-1, CK7, CK20, CDX-2, Melan A, and lymphoid markers. Diagnosis of primary LGNECS requires confirmation of clear margins or need for re-excision, and staging to exclude occult internal primary.

report.source_text: The patient’s health was unaffected by the diagnosis. He has been followed every 6 months with CT/MRI scans for 30 months now, and there is no sign of recurrence or of any other primary neuroendocrine tumour (NET).

clinician.final_diagnosis: primary low-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma of the skin (LGNECS)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his late 30s presented with a 4mm painful subareolar skin nodule present for 5-6 years. Initial excision by GP (suspecting dermatofibroma) revealed on H&E a dermal tumor with solid/organoid pattern, neuroendocrine cytology (oval nuclei, dispersed chromatin, eosinophilic granular cytoplasm), and mitotic count of 8 per 2 mm². Immunohistochemistry confirmed neuroendocrine differentiation (synaptophysin+, CD56+, SATB2+, ISLET-1+, dot-like pan-cytokeratin AE1/AE3+) with low proliferative activity (Ki-67 up to 10%). The profile excluded Merkel cell carcinoma (MCPyV negative), melanoma (despite S-100/SOX-10 positivity, melanoma markers negative), lymphoma (CD45/CD3/CD20 negative), and metastatic carcinomas from lung (TTF-1 negative), GI tract (CK7/CK20/CDX-2 negative), and other sites. Staging with FDG-PET was negative and Gallium-PET identified only benign birthmarks, excluding an internal primary neuroendocrine tumor. Secondary wide local excision (1cm margin) with removal of the birthmarks was performed. After 30 months of surveillance (CT/MRI every 6 months), there was no recurrence and no evidence of an alternative primary neuroendocrine tumor, confirming the diagnosis of primary LGNECS.
